A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldPack by the same authors, retaining the CDiT backbone and LoopNav/RECON evaluations despite substantial revisions. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and appendices were readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original WorldPack results on LoopNav and RECON, component ablations, rollout analyses, and computational measurements. These extend beyond the baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: V2 reports revised WorldPack experiments and original pose-embedding, compression, runtime-scaling, and pooled-FVD analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V1 combines recency-oriented packing with eight retrieved frames selected using a position/orientation score. V2 replaces this with Monte Carlo field-of-view overlap and a temporal penalty, using spatial rankings to allocate compression rates, including the uncompressed slots. The practical configuration changes from 19 frames in a 2.84-frame-equivalent context to 22 frames in a four-frame context (Section 4).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Minecraft LoopNav ABA/ABCA tasks at navigation ranges 5, 15, 30, and 50, plus real-world RECON navigation. Revised history lengths and rollout analyses change procedures within this retained coverage; RECON was already evaluated in v1 Section 6.4.

E2.justification: Oasis, Mineworld, DIAMOND, and NWM remain the main comparators, and packing-only continues as Nearest Frame Packing. V2 adds the retrieval-only control to the rollout curves and replaces NWM with packing/retrieval variants in Figure 3. Its retrieval control uses four FoV-ranked frames, representing WorldMem/Context-as-Memory mechanisms within the shared backbone. The RECON comparison drops Packing only (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4).

E3.justification: V2 equalizes component-ablation context budgets at four frames, changes packed configurations from 19 to 22 visible frames, and changes RECON's initial history from 20 to 80 frames. It extends plotted rollout windows, adds FVD to RECON and component comparisons, and adds pooled evaluation over 144 LoopNav rollouts. Table 1 also revises Mineworld's reported context from 15 to 32 and DIAMOND/NWM from 4 to 32, while retaining their means; this does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond revising the existing packing/retrieval ablations and extending rollout curves, v2 adds camera-pose-embedding removal and temporal/spatiotemporal compression studies (Appendix E). It also measures selection runtime against candidate count (Table 6) and checks whether FVD rankings persist when all 144 trajectories are pooled (Appendix G). These substantially broaden the mechanisms and limitations tested.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates. V2 systematically adds means and standard deviations across evaluation trajectories for SSIM, LPIPS, PSNR, and DreamSim in the main comparisons and ablations, while reporting FVD as a single set-level distance. This substantially expands variability reporting, but neither PDF establishes repeated-training-run counts or uncertainty across seeds.

E6.justification: WorldPack results are extensively replaced: Table 1's ABCA-5 SSIM changes from 0.35 to 0.44, whereas ABA-15 SSIM changes from 0.48 to 0.38, under revised method/context settings. Tables 2 and the RECON table also change, and new ablations and pooled FVD results are added, including WorldPack's 608 versus baseline 872 in Table 13. Efficiency findings change from reduced memory usage to approximately 12% greater usage; these are revised-configuration results, not same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The core mathematical definitions change substantially. V1 Equations 4–9 define a Gaussian-weighted position/direction score without explicit FoV; v2 Equations 6–7 define normalized viewing-frustum intersection volume and a temporal penalty. The separate recent/retrieved-frame allocation in v1 Equations 10–11 becomes spatial-priority allocation in v2 Equations 4–5. The diffusion preliminaries and CDiT complexity argument remain unchanged; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution is redefined from combining trajectory packing with memory retrieval to dynamically controlling compression through spatial relevance. V2's conclusion explicitly locates the contribution in compression-rate allocation rather than spatial scoring itself. Efficiency claims are also qualified: v1's conclusion describes retention without increased computational cost, whereas v2's abstract reports 16% diffusion-inference overhead plus additional selection cost.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's simulator-only limitation, which conflicted with its RECON experiment, with specific limitations involving occlusion, camera-pose availability, and localization errors. Appendix E adds an interpretation linking excessive compression to information loss. Section 6.5 also qualifies computational efficiency through candidate-dependent selection costs, replacing the earlier emphasis on marginal overhead and reduced memory.

D1.justification: V2 fills substantial documentation gaps through Appendices B–D: metric implementations, training/test trajectory counts, RECON eligibility, preprocessing, VAE/backbone configuration, optimizer settings, training and fine-tuning budgets, and H100 hardware. Section 4.2 also specifies overlap sampling and scoring weights. These are largely newly disclosed details; v1's omissions do not establish that all underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work and positions WorldPack as unifying FramePack-style compression with WorldMem/Context-as-Memory retrieval, explicitly attributing spatial scoring to prior work. It adds discussion and citations concerning adaptive tokenization, newer world models, drift correction, and pose estimation. V1's positioning primarily emphasized transferring frame compression into world modeling.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, ablation discussion, limitations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Separate retrieval and packing subsections become a unified spatially-aware-memory section. The appendix is reorganized into Sections A–G, and the LLM-use disclosure moves there from the main text. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn around geometric selection and compression, Algorithm 1 is added, and Figure 3 uses new rollout examples and comparator rows. The ABA-5 bar-chart comparison becomes Table 3; rollout plots change windows, axes, and legends. Numerous training, ablation, and evaluation tables are added, alongside broader typography and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves reproducibility and support for the proposed mechanism. Algorithm 1 and Appendices B–D address major documentation gaps, while equal-context-budget component comparisons, new ablations, trajectory variability reporting, and pooled FVD strengthen experimental interpretation. Computational costs and applicability limitations are more explicit. RECON loses its packing-only control, and changed settings prevent interpreting revised scores as direct performance gains, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial gains in transparency and evidential support.
